<thought>Using the single measurement (6.667 Ω) between terminals A and X1 and the note that the subnetwork contains exactly two resistors where one is twice the other, the only topology that satisfies these constraints is a simple series chain of two resistors. Let the smaller resistor be R1 and the larger (twice) be R2. Then R1 + R2 = 6.667 Ω and R2 = 2·R1, giving R1 ≈ 2.222 Ω and R2 ≈ 4.444 Ω. The series connection can be represented with an internal node (N) between the two resistors, matching the “left‑to‑right” labeling requirement.</thought>
